title: FancyZones “Move newly created windows to their last known zone” causes Adobe Illustrator canvas to open blank on multi-monitor setup

labels.name: Issue-Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: Product-FancyZones
labels.description: Refers to the FancyZones PowerToy

labels.name: Needs-Triage
labels.description: For issues raised to be triaged and prioritized by internal Microsoft teams

body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version

0.99.1

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

Use a multi-monitor setup.
In my case:
Monitor 1: 1080 x 2560, portrait, 100 percent scale
Monitor 2: 2560 x 1080, landscape, 100 percent scale
Monitor 2 is the main display
Open PowerToys Settings.
Go to FancyZones.
Enable FancyZones.
Under Window behavior, enable “Move newly created windows to their last known zone.”
Open Adobe Illustrator.
Open an existing Illustrator document or create a new document.
The Illustrator UI loads normally, and the Layers panel shows the document content.
The document canvas/artboard area appears blank or empty.
Pressing Ctrl + 0 or Ctrl + Alt + 0 does not reveal the artboard.
Turning off “Move newly created windows to their last known zone” fixes the issue.
Turning off the second monitor also fixes the issue.
Reopening the same Illustrator document after disabling that FancyZones setting displays the canvas normally.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Adobe Illustrator documents should open normally with the canvas, artboards, and artwork visible.

FancyZones should move or restore the main application window only when appropriate. It should not interfere with Illustrator’s internal document view, child windows, or canvas rendering.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

When “Move newly created windows to their last known zone” is enabled, Adobe Illustrator opens documents with a blank canvas/artboard area.

The file content is still loaded. The Layers panel shows the artwork, and the contents can be copied into another document. However, the artwork and artboard are not visible in the active document window.

This happens with both existing Illustrator files and newly created documents. It has happened repeatedly over a long period of time. The issue disappears when the FancyZones setting “Move newly created windows to their last known zone” is disabled, or when the second monitor is turned off.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-05-31-23-00-03.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28443785/PowerToysReport_2026-05-31-23-00-03.zip)

### Additional Information

History:
This issue has affected my Illustrator workflow for years. I previously thought it was an Illustrator rendering, GPU, workspace, or preference issue, but I have now isolated it to the FancyZones setting “Move newly created windows to their last known zone.”

FancyZones has existed since the first public PowerToys preview in 2019, and this specific behavior appears tied to FancyZones automatically moving newly opened windows to the last zone location used by that application.

This issue has been going on since i have started using a second monitor with this feature on.

### Other Software

Adobe Illustrator

The issue affects Illustrator document windows/canvas rendering. The Illustrator application UI remains visible, but the document canvas/artboard area becomes blank.

Potentially relevant related behavior:
This may be related to FancyZones treating Illustrator document views, child windows, or internal document windows as newly created windows, then applying last-known-zone positioning in a way that breaks the Illustrator canvas rendering.

body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

Fixes unchecked checkboxes displaying a dark checkmark after a module is disabled and re-enabled, while their stored values remain unchecked.

Closes #50623.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Closes: #50623
- [ ] **Communication:** I've discussed this with core contributors already.
- [x] **Tests:** Ran the existing Settings unit suite (286 passed) and manually verified checkbox rendering and interaction.
- [ ] **Localization:** All end-user-facing strings can be localized.
- [ ] **Dev docs:** Added/updated.
- [ ] **New binaries:** Added on the required places.
- [ ] **Documentation updated:** Linked documentation PR.

## Detailed Description

The affected unchecked glyph can receive the generic animated-icon state `Normal` after re-enable, instead of `NormalOff`. `src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/Behaviors/CheckBoxAnimationBehavior.cs` corrects this state only when the checkbox is unchecked and its glyph uses WinUI's `AnimatedAcceptVisualSource`. The behavior detaches on unload and reattaches when the control loads or its template changes.

`src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/SettingsXAML/App.xaml` applies the behavior to standard and descriptive checkboxes. WinUI's checkbox template, glyph brushes, and hover/pressed states remain native, preserving enabled check/uncheck animations. Checked and indeterminate states are excluded from the correction. No theme brush overrides are required.

## Validation Steps Performed

Tested revision: `a0ba24dd72` (x64 Debug).

- Built Settings UI and `Settings.UI.UnitTests` with the repository build scripts, x64 Debug: both exit code 0, zero warnings and errors.
- Manually verified the final build on FancyZones and PowerDisplay: unchecked boxes remain empty after Off → On; checked boxes remain correct. FancyZones' descriptive checkbox also behaves correctly.
- Manually verified mouse and Space-key checking/unchecking, enabled animations, hover, and navigation away and back.
- Manually verified Quick Accent's checked/unchecked/mixed language selection, rapid module toggling, initially disabled pages, light/dark/system/high-contrast theme changes while enabled and disabled, and system animations disabled. Also spot-checked Always On Top and Advanced Paste.

body: ## Summary of the Pull Request This PR improves Peek's file navigation by implementing reuse of compatible Previewers instead of always disposing and recreating them for every new item. This removes the 'white flash' when advancing through files, which is especially problematic for rapid navigation. Currently, `ImagePreviewer` and `UnsupportedFilePreviewer` support reuse, so I consider this a partial fix for issue #34515. However, this update of `ImagePreviewer` will likely be most impactful for user-facing issues with flicker because of the tendency to quickly flick through images when previewing an album. ## PR Checklist - [x] Closes: #50019 - [x] Closes: #50016 - [ ] Closes: #xxx (Partial fix for #34515) - [ ] **Communication:** I've discussed this with core contributors already. If the work hasn't been agreed, this work might be rejected - [x] **Tests:** Added/updated and all pass - [ ] **Localization:** All end-user-facing strings can be localized - [ ] **Dev docs:** Added/updated - [ ] **New binaries:** Added on the required places - [ ] [JSON for signing](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/ESRPSigning_core.json) for new binaries - [ ] [WXS for installer](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/installer/PowerToysSetup/Product.wxs) for new binaries and localization folder - [ ] [YML for CI pipeline](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/ci/templates/build-powertoys-steps.yml) for new test projects - [ ] [YML for signed pipeline](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/release.yml) - [ ] **Documentation updated:** If checked, please file a pull request on [our docs repo](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-uwp/tree/docs/hub/powertoys) and link it here: #xxx ## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments - Added a reuse contract for previewers with `IPreviewerSupportsReuse.Rebind(IFileSystemItem item, double scalingFactor)`. The behaviour is implemented in `ImagePreviewer` and `UnsupportedFilePreviewer` for now. - Updated the navigation flow in `FilePreview` to: - Detect compatible previewer type - Reuse previewers that support item rebinding - Only recreate/dispose a previewer when the type is incompatible - Refactored `PreviewerFactory` to reduce duplicated decision logic and make it open to unit testing: - Unified previewer definitions in a single collection instead of a large if/else ladder. - `GetCompatiblePreviewerType()` and `Create()` use the definition collection - Constructor overloads which support `IPreviewSettings` injection and pre-prepared mock-Previewer definitions - Made `CreateDefaultPreviewer()` static, as it only depends upon the passed-in item - Added a new `DoubleBufferedImageControl` control, which uses a back-buffer to hold the loading image and supports swapping between the front- and back-buffer images immediately. Cross-fading was also implemented but removed as there were rendering issues when the window resized between images. If we ever implement a full-screen Peek option, this could be reintroduced relatively easily. - Minor amendment to `LoadFullQualityImageAsync()` to defer setting Preview until the bitmap is actually loaded. This avoids potentially binding a loading/blank frame and makes the transition between images effectively atomic from the UI's perspective. - Small update to `IsPreviewVisible` in `FilePreview.xaml.cs` for ImagePreviewer so null Previews are not regarded as visible. As above, this guard prevents partially loaded images from being shown, making the instant swap between fully loaded images possible. - Updated the width and height calculations in `WindowExtensions.CenterOnMonitor()` to reduce the possibility of small 'seams' of background pixels showing through between the image edge and window border. @Jay-o-Way - I hope this fixes the issue you refer to in the code: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/3d0c3bdb294f96e2e2907dd9fcd7ba363ed0f8e8/src/modules/peek/Peek.UI/PeekXAML/MainWindow.xaml.cs#L293 Please let me know. - New unit tests to exercise the reusable previewer model and the `Rebind()` call. Currently, I'm creating custom previewers in the unit tests, but `ImagePreviewer` could potentially be tested against directly in integration test(s) in the future. ## Validation Steps Performed ### Unit tests All existing and new unit tests pass: ### Manual testing - Confirmed that images, music files, videos and folders open as before, can be navigated through and deleted (where supported) - Navigated fast through images to confirm that the 'white flash' issue was mitigated - Navigated through images with differing dimensions - Checked image display through CLI mode - Navigated through a large folder of images to check that memory usage was unaffected ### Screen recordings #### Before (warning - flashing images): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ade365c-c873-4c5f-9fa2-388eac312ea2 #### After: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e571701-7b54-4a8d-97fb-2fade885ce44 ### Update Updated with fixes following PR review. More information in [the comment below](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/49963#issuecomment-5348491726). ### Update 2 Updated with race condition fixes, many more unit tests, resource string formatting and retrieval consolidation and navigation timing improvement. More information in [the comment below](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/49963#issuecomment-5589166423). ### Update 3 Updated with further fixes following review, refactored out new helpers to expose more internals to unit testing, added further tests because I keep breaking new and interesting things. More information in [the comment below](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/49963#issuecomment-5925895198).

title: Workspaces: launch automatically at Windows sign-in, with configurable start delay

labels.name: Needs-Triage
labels.description: For issues raised to be triaged and prioritized by internal Microsoft teams

labels.name: Product-Workspaces
labels.description: Refers to the Workspaces utility

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Workspaces can already start a group of apps with saved position, size, window state (e.g. maximized), CLI arguments and admin rights. What is missing is a way to start a workspace automatically at Windows sign-in, with a start delay.

Proposal:

1. A per-workspace option "Launch at sign-in" (e.g. next to "Create desktop shortcut" / "Move existing windows").
2. A configurable start delay, either per workspace (e.g. 0 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min) or, ideally, per app within the workspace, so that apps start staggered instead of all at once.
3. Optional: an option to start the apps one after another with a fixed interval.

The existing per-app data model (position, state, arguments) would only need one additional field, "delay".

### Scenario when this would be used?

After sign-in, many programs (cloud sync, mail client, messengers, backup tools, CAD/slicer software, music player) start at the same time and compete for disk, CPU and network. The system stays sluggish for minutes, and windows end up in random places.

With Workspaces I can already define where each app should be placed and in which state. But I still have to start the workspace manually after every login. Windows itself offers no good alternative:

- Settings > Apps > Startup and shell:startup only allow enabling/disabling, there is no per-app delay.
- The "Run: minimized/maximized" setting of a shortcut is ignored by many apps.
- The only workaround is a Task Scheduler task (trigger "At log on" + "Delay task for") that launches the Workspaces desktop shortcut. That works, but it is a manual, fragile setup outside of PowerToys and has to be maintained separately for every workspace.

Built-in autostart with delay would make Workspaces a complete replacement for startup scripts: the desktop is usable right after login, the load is spread out, and every app ends up where it belongs.

### Supporting information

Current workaround: create the desktop shortcut for the workspace, then use Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) with trigger "At log on" and "Delay task for" (advanced settings), action = start the shortcut.

Third-party tools such as Startup Delayer offer per-app delays, but they know nothing about Workspaces layouts.

body: ## Summary of the Pull Request This PR makes Shortcut Guide's index generation resilient against malformed, corrupt, missing or inaccessible files. This includes broken symlinks, locked files, or manifests with missing fields. Previously, any issue during index creation would result in **PowerToys.ShortcutGuide.IndexYmlGenerator.exe** terminating with exit code **-532462766** (unhandled exception), which aborted index creation. Additionally, if an incomplete or schema-mismatched YAML file was partially indexed, null entries would be added, poisoning the **index.yml** file. In those instances, `ManifestInterpreter.GetAllCurrentApplicationIds()` would throw unhandled `NullReferenceException` or `ArgumentNullException` upon activation, causing Shortcut Guide windows to flash briefly and immediately crash/disappear. A separate PR will follow to correct the underlying reasons behind why corrupt/empty/incomplete YAML files may be occurring. ## PR Checklist - [x] Closes: #50354 - [ ] **Communication:** I've discussed this with core contributors already. If the work hasn't been agreed, this work might be rejected - [x] **Tests:** Added/updated and all pass - [ ] **Localization:** All end-user-facing strings can be localized - [ ] **Dev docs:** Added/updated - [ ] **New binaries:** Added on the required places - [ ] [JSON for signing](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/ESRPSigning_core.json) for new binaries - [ ] [WXS for installer](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/installer/PowerToysSetup/Product.wxs) for new binaries and localization folder - [ ] [YML for CI pipeline](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/ci/templates/build-powertoys-steps.yml) for new test projects - [ ] [YML for signed pipeline](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/release.yml) - [ ] **Documentation updated:** If checked, please file a pull request on [our docs repo](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-uwp/tree/docs/hub/powertoys) and link it here: #xxx ## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments ### 1. Diagnosis For the indexer crash: if users added custom manifests or symlinked dotfiles (as in #50354), any inaccessible file or YAML parsing failure threw an unhandled exception in the index generator exe, aborting the run. To make matters worse, the index generation code deleted an existing **index.yml** file _before_ processing the manifest files, so any unhandled exception would result in the index file being wiped, even if it was correct. For the UI "flash-then-disappear" crash: if a manifest with missing fields or an empty document (or one with only comments) was deserialized into a `ShortcutFile` with one or more null properties: - During foreground window evaluation, `ManifestInterpreter.GetAllCurrentApplicationIds()` called `filter.EndsWith(".exe")` on a **null** filter, resulting in an unhandled `NullReferenceException`. - If a manifest lacked `PackageName`, a null entry was written to **index.yml**. When `ManifestInterpreter.GetAllCurrentApplicationIds()` evaluated matching apps, assigning to `applicationIds[app]` threw an unhandled `ArgumentNullException` because Dictionary keys cannot be null. - Because `GetAllCurrentApplicationIds()` is called when the guide opens, these uncaught exceptions crashed the UI thread immediately after the window appeared, causing the "flash-then-disappear" symptom. ### 2. Manifest validation and indexer robustness improvements - Wrapped manifest parsing in `ManifestIndexGenerator` with a try/catch to catch and log non-fatal file access and parsing issues (IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException, YamlException, NullReferenceException). Corrupt or locked files are logged and skipped, allowing remaining valid manifests to be indexed. - Added explicit `string.IsNullOrWhitespace()` checks for `ShortcutFile.WindowFilter` and `ShortcutFile.PackageName` to skip any files which could cause the previously-mentioned index poisoning. - Removed the upfront deletion of **index.yml** and guarded the file enumeration against parsing it. The file is overwritten by the final `File.WriteAllText()` call at the end of the routine - the delete was never needed. ### 3. Separation of concerns and refactoring - Extracted the entry point into **Program.cs** `Main()` with logger initialisation, top-level execution handling and exit code reporting back to the caller. - Renamed the generator class to `ManifestIndexGenerator` to eliminate CA1724 warnings and namespace/type name collision (**ShortcutGuide.IndexYmlGenerator.IndexYmlGenerator**). - Added a `CreateIndexYmlFile(string path)` overload, allowing in-process invocation against temporary directories for isolated testing without modifying user app data. The exe name, build output location and CLI contract remain 100% unchanged. ### 4. Unit tests - Added unit tests under new `IndexGeneratorTests` covering: valid manifest indexing and output verification; resilience against malformed YAML syntax; graceful handling of empty/whitespace-only/missing field manifests; skipping and overwriting existing **index.yml** files; and correct grouping and deduplication of packages containing the same `WindowFilter`. ## Validation Steps Performed - Ran all new and existing unit tests: - Verified that corrupted manifests and empty files are skipped gracefully with error logs while all valid manifests are correctly indexed into **index.yml**. - Verified that no null records were written to **index.yml**, preventing downstream unhandled exceptions in **ShortcutGuide.UI**. - Verified that new logs are correctly written for all classes of errors and warnings: ``` [04:21:35.8089878] [Info] Program.cs::Main::15 Starting Shortcut Guide index file generation... body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Enable the Shortcut Guide to either
- index user-added shortcut manifests inside subfolders of `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\KeyboardShortcuts\`, OR
- index symlinked manifests inside said folder above (with or without subfolder support).

### Scenario when this would be used?

Users could create a separate folder for their own generated / hand-written shortcut manifests, which they could easily and selectively maintain i.e. with a dotfile manager like chezmoi, a plain VCS like git, or a cloud backup utility like OneDrive or Google Drive.
This solves the problem of constantly backing up the whole `KeyboardShortcuts` folder or prefixing user-custom files with something and searching for them afterwards. Plus it would be structurally cleaner (either the subfolder solution or "a separate folder's contents symlinked" solution).

### Supporting information

#### Current state, logs

When a new manifest is added inside a subfolder, ShortcutGuide does not check and index them at all.

When these manifests are symlinked (using pwsh command `New-Item -type SymbolicLink ...`) into the `KeyboardShortcuts` folder, the guide throws an error when initialized, and does not proceed with index generation:

```log
// %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\ShortcutGuide\Log_2026-09-03.log

[12:59:43.7620459] [Error] Program.cs::Main::101
    Index generation failed with exit code -532462766. There may be a corrupt shortcuts file in "C:\Users\Daniel\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\KeyboardShortcuts".
```

Folder structure looks like this:

```tree
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\KeyboardShortcuts
¦   +Godot.Godot.en-US.yml
¦   +Microsoft.OutlookForWindows.en-US.yml
¦   +ON1.PhotoRAW.en-US.yml

¦   +WindowsNT.Notepad.en-US.yml
¦   +WindowsNT.Shell.en-US.yml
¦   ...
¦   
+---custom
        +WindowsNT.Notepad-custom.yml
```

#### Background

I use ShortcutGuide to constantly remind myself of the handy-dandy keybinds set inside apps I use, but I also have custom shortcuts for said applications. I recently noticed that this PowerToy has this functionality and I wanted to improve this cool tool, because I use a config/dotfiles manager (*chezmoi*, which is basically *git* with *go* templates and extra steps) and I want to tidy and sync said shortcuts' guides to my other devices.

title: feat(mouseutils): add haptic feedback to Cursor Wrap

## Summary of the Pull Request

Adds haptic feedback after Cursor Wrap successfully moves the pointer to the opposite screen edge.

The implementation uses `Windows.Devices.Haptics.InputHapticsManager` and plays the **Grow** waveform once per completed wrap. Because Cursor Wrap normally handles movement on a background low-level hook thread, `src/modules/MouseUtils/CursorWrap/dllmain.cpp` creates invisible one-pixel edge input windows while wrapping is active. The physical edge event is delivered to the module's thread before the pointer transition, allowing Windows to route feedback to the active haptic mouse.

## Summary of the Pull Request

Adds a support-oriented PowerShell cleanup tool for recovering systems where per-user and per-machine PowerToys registrations cause their bootstrappers to block each other. The tool enumerates known PowerToys MSI products, removes active products directly through `msiexec`, and invokes trusted cached WiX bootstrappers to clear bundle registrations.

Related to #43774. The same mixed-scope failure was also reported in duplicate #49800.

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

The script is PowerShell 5.1-compatible and uses `SupportsShouldProcess`, confirmation, and `-WhatIf`. Discovery can run without elevation; actual cleanup requires 64-bit elevated PowerShell.

Safety is intentionally conservative: MSI caches and bundle executables must have a valid Microsoft signature and PowerToys identity, and bundle records must match the exact PowerToys upgrade code. Failures are aggregated, MSI logs are retained, and reboot-required exit codes are reported.

PowerToys settings, logs, update downloads, and telemetry state are preserved by default. `-RemoveSettings` additionally removes the current user's settings and registry data. The tool never removes WebView2 or administrator policies.

Per-user installations belonging to other Windows profiles must be removed by running the tool from each affected profile. Missing or untrusted caches are reported rather than executed or deleted.

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

`src\settings-ui\Settings.UI\Assets\Settings\Scripts\DisableModule.ps1` previously toggled deletion at any line containing either GUID and wrote the result even when an opening marker had no closing marker. An interrupted enable operation or manually damaged marker could therefore remove all trailing user functions while reporting success.

The removal script now:

- Recognizes whole-line opening and closing comments, not GUID substrings or examples inside strings/block comments.
- Requires non-nested pairs with matching GUIDs. Both legacy `34de4b3d-13a8-4540-b76d-b9e8d3851756` and current `f45873b3-b655-43a6-b217-97c00aa0db58` blocks remain supported, including multiple complete blocks of either version.
- Rejects missing, mixed, nested, or duplicate boundaries before any write, even if an earlier block was valid. The entire original file remains unchanged on these refusals.
- Checks lossless decoding and preserves unrelated content, BOM, mixed CRLF/LF/CR endings, and final-newline state. Writes a completed temporary sibling before replacing the profile instead of truncating the original first.
- Prints explicit failure diagnostics to stdout, which the existing Settings process wrapper captures, and rethrows the error. Neither existing success token is emitted on refusal or I/O failure. Both successful-removal and no-instance messages remain unchanged for `CmdNotFoundViewModel`.

`src\settings-ui\Settings.UI.UnitTests\Scripts\DisableModule.Tests.ps1` adds focused coverage using the repository's existing Pester mechanism. Every invocation shadows `$PROFILE` with a disposable `$TestDrive` fixture; profile contents are never executed.

**Behavioral risk:** This deliberately refuses to guess when recognized boundaries are malformed; users must repair those markers before removal. Lossy decoding and filesystem replacement failures are surfaced rather than falling back to a destructive write. Replacement was exercised on the local Windows filesystem, not every redirected/network profile location.

**Scope:** No changes to prerequisite detection, enable/upgrade scripts, package installation, process execution, Settings schemas, GPO, elevation, or installer behavior. This is profile-boundary safety, not the separate uninstall behavior tracked in #31039.

body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

After updating PowerToys, my usual FancyZones workflow stopped working, and it took me a while to figure out that FancyZones wasn't the culprit.

My habit: with "Override Windows Snap" enabled, I focus a window, hold down the Win key, and tap Left/Right arrow repeatedly to cycle the window through my zones until it lands where I want it. I've worked this way for a long time. Holding Win for the whole sequence is the natural way to do it.

Since the update, the first Win+Arrow press moves the window, but before I can press the arrow a second time, numbered boxes appear over my taskbar icons — the Shortcut Guide — and subsequent arrow presses stop moving the window. From my perspective, it looked like FancyZones was broken. 

What's actually happening is that the update enabled Shortcut Guide (or reset its activation to the Win-key long press), and my sustained Win hold crosses the activation threshold between arrow presses. Once the guide appears, it swallows the keys.

Disabling the Shortcut Guide module restored the FancyZones behavior completely, so I have my workaround. But I'd suggest the defaults deserve a look: a long-press activation on the Win key is inherently in tension with FancyZones' own Win+Arrow feature, since that feature invites the user to hold Win continuously. Two modules in the same suite shouldn't fight over the same key out of the box — or at minimum, the guide could suppress activation when a Win+combo has already fired during the current hold.

### Scenario when this would be used?

FancyZones is a great tool and the new Shorcut Guide V2's default activation interferes with my use of it.

### Supporting information

PowerToys Release v0.101.2362.0
OS Name	Microsoft Windows 11 Pro
Version	10.0.26200 Build 26200

body: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.101.2362.0 — Stable; new WinUI 3 editor enabled (useNewEditor: true) ### Installation method GitHub — installed from [GitHub release v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/releases/tag/v0.101.2362.0). ### Area(s) with issue? Keyboard Manager ### Steps to reproduce Installation details: machine-wide installation under C:\Program Files\PowerToys; installed from the GitHub release linked above. An existing configuration has three mappings with the trigger Ctrl (Left) + Shift (Left) + N (162;160;78): | Scope | Action | | --- | --- | | Global | Open Chrome | | code.exe | Remap to Ctrl (Left) + Shift (Right) + N | | parsecd.exe | Remap to Ctrl (Left) + Shift (Right) + N | 1. Open this existing configuration in the new Keyboard Manager editor. 2. Edit the global Open app mapping. 3. Keep the trigger unchanged and leave Only apply to a specific app unchecked. 4. Observe the Duplicate remapping validation error. The observed screenshot shows the error in Edit remapping, with Allow chords checked. This configuration previously worked; the exact last working version is unknown. Suggested minimal reproduction: one global shortcut mapping and one app-specific override of the same trigger, then edit the global mapping. This reduced two-entry case has not been tested separately. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior Allow a global shortcut mapping and app-specific overrides with the same trigger. In a matching app, the app-specific mapping should take precedence; elsewhere, the global mapping should apply. This behavior is described in the [Keyboard Manager engine documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/doc/devdocs/modules/keyboardmanager/keyboardmanager.md): app-specific shortcut handling runs before global shortcut handling so the app-specific variant takes precedence. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The editor displays: > Duplicate remapping — This key or shortcut is already remapped. There is exactly one mapping per scope for this trigger. Both default.json and editorSettings.json confirm these distinct scopes; all three editor entries are active. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information Windows 11 Home, 26H2, build 26300.9550, 64-bit. Machine-wide installation under C:\Program Files\PowerToys; installed from GitHub release v0.101.2362.0. Evidence: user-supplied screenshot and read-only inspection of the current configuration. No mappings were changed during investigation. No separate runtime test or preview-version test was performed. **Likely cause:** [ValidationHelper.IsDuplicateMapping in v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs#L202-L209) uses this app-scope predicate: ```csharp string.IsNullOrEmpty(settings.Shortcut.TargetApp) || string.IsNullOrEmpty(appName) || settings.Shortcut.TargetApp == appName ``` When editing a global mapping, appName is empty, so matching triggers from every app scope count as duplicates. Here, the count is three and exceeds the edit-mode tolerance of one. **Existing reports and fixes checked:** #48749 concerns entries being duplicated on save, rather than this global/app-scope false positive. #49710 was closed by merged PR #50265, which changes edit-mode identity exclusion and filters inactive entries. However, [the current main-branch implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs#L209-L225) still has the same empty-app OR predicate. That related fix does not address this scope comparison. Suggested correction: compare normalized application scopes for duplicate detection, preserving global mappings and app-specific overrides as distinct while rejecting duplicate triggers within the same scope. Relevant configuration excerpt (optional launch arguments omitted): ```json { "remapShortcuts": { "global": [{ "originalKeys": "162;160;78", "exactMatch": false, "operationType": 1, "runProgramFilePath": "C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" }], "appSpecific": [ { "originalKeys": "162;160;78", "newRemapKeys": "162;161;78", "exactMatch": false, "operationType": 0, "targetApp": "code.exe" }, { "originalKeys": "162;160;78", "newRemapKeys": "162;161;78", "exactMatch": false, "operationType": 0, "targetApp": "parsecd.exe" } ] } } ``` ### Other Software Google Chrome, Visual Studio Code (code.exe), and Parsec (parsecd.exe). Their versions were not collected; the observed failure is editor validation. ### Screenshot

title: CmdPal: show GPU temperature in Performance Monitor using D3DKMT

labels.name: Product-Command Palette
labels.description: Refers to the Command Palette utility

body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

Performance Monitor currently shows `--` for GPU temperature because the value is never collected. This change reads the temperature through Windows' D3DKMT interface and displays it in the existing GPU details view.

The approach is similar to Task Manager and uses the standard WDDM interface. It does not require an additional vendor driver, vendor SDK, or hardware-monitoring library. The installed graphics driver still needs to expose the temperature through WDDM.

Related to #46434 and #50792. This implements GPU temperature in the details view; CPU temperature and additional Dock metrics remain follow-up work.

## PR Checklist

- [ ] **Communication:** Maintainer feedback is requested on this implementation and the CPU temperature follow-up below.
- [x] **Tests:** Added temperature tests; all 107 Performance Monitor tests pass locally.
- [x] **Localization:** No new end-user-facing strings; reuses the existing temperature field and unavailable indicator.
- [x] **Dev docs:** API units, native layouts, and adapter-handle lifetime are explained in code comments.
- [x] **New binaries:** Not applicable; no new binaries, packages, or test projects.
- [x] **Documentation updated:** Not applicable; no public documentation changes are required.

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

- Matches temperature readings to the existing GPU LUID, so integrated and discrete GPUs remain separate.
- Uses `D3DKMTOpenAdapterFromLuid`, `D3DKMTQueryAdapterInfo` with `KMTQAITYPE_ADAPTERPERFDATA`, and `D3DKMTCloseAdapter`. Converts the temperature from tenths of Celsius.
- Samples on the existing one-second update cycle. Driver calls run outside the lock used by UI accessors.
- Clears the previous reading when a query fails or returns an unavailable/invalid value, and retries on the next update.
- Uses source-generated P/Invoke for Native AOT compatibility. Adapter handles are closed after each query rather than retained across driver resets.

API reference: [D3DKMT_ADAPTER_PERFDATA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/d3dkmthk/ns-d3dkmthk-_d3dkmt_adapter_perfdata).

## Validation Steps Performed

- Built the Performance Monitor extension, its tests, and Command Palette UI as x64 Debug using the repository build script.
- Ran all 107 Performance Monitor tests: 107 passed, 0 failed. New coverage includes native structure layouts, temperature conversion, GPU mapping, and clearing/recovering unavailable readings.
- Tested on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU. A native Windows SDK probe returned 52.1°C; the compiled extension's sampling and formatting path returned `52 °C` across three consecutive updates. Intel integrated graphics returned an unavailable value and displayed `--`.
- `git diff --check` passes.

Hardware validation is currently limited to this x64 laptop. ARM64, other GPU vendors, and real sleep/resume or driver-reset scenarios have not been tested. Linked display adapters currently use physical adapter index 0, matching the existing one-entry-per-LUID model.

## Concern about the CPU temperature follow-up

I would like to add CPU package/core temperature next. That needs a different approach: I expect it to require vendor-specific hardware access and a supporting driver or SDK dependency. For example, [Intel PCM uses an MSR kernel driver on Windows](https://github.com/intel/pcm/blob/master/doc/WINDOWS_HOWTO.md). ACPI thermal-zone readings cannot reliably be presented as CPU temperature, as discussed in the review of #48639.

Would a vendor-specific driver or SDK dependency be acceptable for a separate CPU temperature implementation in PowerToys? If so, is there a preferred approach or existing dependency I should use before starting that work?



Further discussion of the CPU temperature implementation and its driver/SDK dependencies is tracked in #50916. Please continue that discussion in the issue; this PR remains focused on GPU temperature.

title: [Keyboard Manager] Backup/restore omits editorSettings.json, leaving new editor settings stale

labels.name: Issue-Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: Needs-Triage
labels.description: For issues raised to be triaged and prioritized by internal Microsoft teams

body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 — Stable; new WinUI 3 editor enabled (useNewEditor: true). Restored backup manifest: v0.100.2.

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager, Settings

### Steps to reproduce

Installation details: machine-wide installation under `C:\Program Files\PowerToys`, installed from [GitHub release v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/releases/tag/v0.101.2362.0). Version/channel and installation details match my existing report #50933.

**Observed restore scenario:**

1. The destination PC already has a new Keyboard Manager editor configuration in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\Keyboard Manager\editorSettings.json`, with `useNewEditor: true`.
2. Restore a PowerToys backup whose global Open app shortcut has different Chrome arguments and launch options from that existing editor configuration.
3. PowerToys restores `Keyboard Manager\default.json` and restarts.
4. Compare the restored runtime shortcut with the same global shortcut in `editorSettings.json`.

For the global left Ctrl + left Shift + N shortcut, the observed post-restore values were:

| Setting | Restored runtime `default.json` | Existing `editorSettings.json` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome arguments | `--profile-directory="Profile Local" https://www.google.com/` | `--profile-directory="LocalProfile" https://www.google.com/` |
| Already running | `runProgramAlreadyRunningAction: 1` (Start another) | `IfRunningAction: 0` (Show window) |
| Window visibility | `runProgramStartWindowType: 3` (Maximized) | `Visibility: 0` (Normal) |

The restore log specifically records `Keyboard Manager\default.json` being updated from backup. The Keyboard Manager engine subsequently logged launching Chrome with the restored `Profile Local` arguments, confirming that the **runtime restore succeeded**.

The extracted backup manifest lists `default.json` but does not list `editorSettings.json`. The existing editor file retained its older save timestamp and values.

**Deterministic filter test, run separately without changing live settings:**

The installed `WinUI3Apps\backup_restore_settings.json` includes `*Keyboard Manager\default.json` and generic `*settings.json`, but no explicit pattern for `editorSettings.json`.

This PowerShell test uses the same wildcard-to-regex conversion as the backup implementation:

```powershell
$path = 'C:\Example\Microsoft\PowerToys\Keyboard Manager\editorSettings.json'
$regex = '^' + [regex]::Escape('*settings.json').Replace('\*', '.*') + '$'
[regex]::IsMatch($path, $regex) # False
[regex]::IsMatch($path, $regex, [System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexOptions]::IgnoreCase) # True
```

Testing that path against **every installed include pattern** also returned no match.

The actual restore and saved-file mismatch were inspected. A separate clean-install UI reproduction and a save-from-stale-editor overwrite test were not performed.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

After restoring a backup, the new Keyboard Manager editor should agree with the restored runtime mappings and launch options.

Backup/restore should either preserve the required new editor state or reliably reconcile existing editor state with the restored runtime configuration.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The runtime settings restore successfully, while the separate persisted new editor settings remain stale. This leaves two conflicting saved representations of the same shortcut and creates a risk that a subsequent editor save could restore old values. That overwrite risk has not been tested in this report.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToys-KeyboardManager-backup-sanitized-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32935374/PowerToys-KeyboardManager-backup-sanitized-evidence.zip)

### Additional Information

- Windows 11 Home, 26H2, OS build **26300.9550**, 64-bit.
- New editor enabled: `useNewEditor: true`.
- Inspection and filter test performed October 1, 2026.
- Workaround used: with editors closed, back up both files and correct only the affected shortcut's arguments and launch options in both saved representations. Unrelated mappings were preserved.
- Attached a focused, sanitized evidence ZIP containing the pre-fix affected-shortcut fields, relevant official-report log excerpts, and installed backup include filters. This is not the complete unmodified bug-report ZIP. The official report was generated after the workaround; pre-fix values come from preserved originals. Unrelated settings, personal paths, and system inventories were omitted.

**Likely cause:**

1. [Backup include rules in v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/backup_restore_settings.json) omit an explicit `editorSettings.json` pattern. The same rules are present in v0.100.2.
2. [IsIncludeFile / GetSettingsFiles](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/SettingsBackupAndRestoreUtils.cs#L526-L567) use `Regex.IsMatch` without `IgnoreCase`. The capital **S** in `editorSettings.json` therefore prevents a match with lowercase `*settings.json`.
3. [SettingsManager.LoadSettings in the installed release](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Settings/SettingsManager.cs#L50-L75) imports native mappings when the editor file does not exist, but reads the existing editor file when it is present.

The filter omission is reproduced directly; the explanation of how it causes the stale editor state follows from the inspected files and release source.

Please consider explicitly including the editor file with suitable restore semantics, and/or reconciling editor state after a runtime configuration restore. Merely creating another standard backup still excludes the editor file under these rules.

### Other Software

Google Chrome (used for the Open app shortcut).

title: [Shortcut Guide] Manifest index creation refactor and bug fixing

labels.name: Product-Shortcut Guide
labels.description: Refers to the Shortcut Guide PowerToy

body: ## Summary of the Pull Request This PR refactors the index generation and startup pipeline of Shortcut Guide, improving launch speed, removing redundancy and fixing concurrency issues. Several related bug fixes - including for a crash bug and for startup window flicker - are also included. It builds upon the prior PR #50497, which centred on fixing the lack of error handling and file checking in the index generation project. The commits from this PR are the latest 3. (I couldn't create a stacked PR because I don't have the necessary permissions, sorry.) This PR is focused on the manifest file index creation and initial application startup and includes a further 12 unit tests on top of the 5 from the earlier PR. ## PR Checklist - [x] Closes: #50570 - [x] Closes: #50571 - [x] Closes: #50586 - [x] Closes: #50588 - [x] Closes: #50590 - [ ] **Communication:** I've discussed this with core contributors already. If the work hasn't been agreed, this work might be rejected - [x] **Tests:** Added/updated and all pass - [ ] **Localization:** All end-user-facing strings can be localized - [ ] **Dev docs:** Added/updated - [ ] **New binaries:** Added on the required places - [ ] [JSON for signing](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/ESRPSigning_core.json) for new binaries - [ ] [WXS for installer](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/installer/PowerToysSetup/Product.wxs) for new binaries and localization folder - [ ] [YML for CI pipeline](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/ci/templates/build-powertoys-steps.yml) for new test projects - [ ] [YML for signed pipeline](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/release.yml) - [ ] **Documentation updated:** If checked, please file a pull request on [our docs repo](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-uwp/tree/docs/hub/powertoys) and link it here: #xxx ## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments ### Fixes - Fixed crash bug caused by the `_getAppIdsTask` Task in `MainPaneControl` being `Dispose`d while it was still active. If the application was closed and then reopened immediately, this would cause the crash because two threads were attempting to update the nav items list concurrently. Tasks typically don't need to be disposed of manually. To fix the underlying issue, an invocation generation counter was added to the `MainPaneControl`, so an old Task can never update a newer instance of the control. A log entry is added when this is detected and mitigated. - Hardened `MainPaneControl.InitializeNavItemsAsync` against a latent null-reference: the background app-id task is now captured to a local variable before use, so it can no longer be cleared concurrently (by `Hide()`/`OnUnloaded()`) between the null-check and the subsequent `await`. - Fixed the UI flashing immediately upon first activation before the full overlay window is shown. This was a combination of an event ordering issue, the `Visibility` property of `MainPane` being set to `Visible` too soon (in the `Loaded` handler), and the module runner passing `SW_SHOW` instead of `SW_HIDE`. - The PowerToys hotkeys manifest file is now generated _before_ the index file is created. Previously, this order was reversed, meaning Shortcut Guide had to be restarted twice to pick up any PowerToys shortcut changes by the user. - `PowerToysShortcutsPopulator.Populate()` now diffs its generated content against what's on disk and only writes if it actually changed. - Fixed the foreground window only being logged at application start instead of when the shortcut window is actually requested. The HWND/module/exe information is now logged each time Shortcut Guide is triggered. - The index file writing is now atomic. Previously, it was possible for the UI project to read a part-written index file, leading to an exception. Now, the index file is created as a temporary file before being `Move()`d to its destination. ### Performance - Manifest files are not copied if the bundled file has the same modified date or older. - The index file is not recreated if all manifest files in the destination folder are older than it. - In the UI project, the YamlDotNet `Deserializer` is no longer created for each file's parsing - a shared class-level `Deserializer` is used instead, and set to `Lazy<>` so we don't pay for the setup cost if it isn't used. - In `PowerToysShortcutsPopulator.HotkeySettingsToYaml`, we now use a `StringBuilder` instead of concatenating string instances when creating shortcut entries for YAML, saving allocations and time, especially as there are already hundreds of shortcuts to process. - The index generator is called in-process instead of shelling out to an exe via `Process.Start()`. Shelling out can cost more than 150 ms, and the UI cannot be displayed until this step is complete. The index generator exe is still available for external callers, and is now just a thin wrapper around calling the shared `CreateIndexYmlFile()`. - Manifest index generation now processes the headers only, and uses a small custom deserializer which is `Span`-based and allocation-free. Previously, YamlDotNet deserialized each manifest file completely, including the shortcuts, which were not needed. Manifest file opening and processing is done in parallel, which helps to mitigate the cost of anti-virus scanning of any newly-copied manifest files. - Index file serialization is now a few lines of `StringBuilder` code and removes the need for YamlDotNet's serializer, saving startup memory and time. - In the UI project, logging the foreground window is done via a background Task, as it calls relatively expensive process-interrogation APIs. - `GetCachedIndexYamlFile()` is called once in `GetAllCurrentApplicationIds()` and `IndexFile` is cached, instead of every time a lookup happens. The file does not change after generating, so loading and deserializing the data each time is not required. - `Task`s used instead of `Thread`s (see below). ### Manifest Index Generator project - Now free of dependencies. The project is now AOT compilation compliant and publishing an AOT compiled version has been tested. - `ManifestIndexGenerator` is shared between the console utility (`PowerToys.ShortcutGuide.IndexYmlGenerator.exe`) and the desktop application. - The manifest file path is owned by this project now, under `IndexYmlGenerator.ManifestIndexGenerator.DefaultManifestsPath`. This means the UI project dependency can be removed, as it was only in place for this single path. - The new manifest header parser and index file writer allowed for the removal of the YamlDotNet dependency and a significant increase in speed. - A `Managed.Common.Logger`-compliant mini-logger was added, so CLI-callers can get logs output by file and/or via the console. - The AOT-compiled exe runs in 4 ms instead of 900 ms or more, including file reading, parsing and generating the index for 43 files. ### Asynchrony Changed `new Thread()` calls with TAP throughout: 1. Manifest and Index Generation (Program.cs) - Old: Used a raw `new Thread()` for file copying/generation, which was later synchronously blocked on the UI thread using `.Join()` during the window's initialization. - New: Converted to a fire-and-forget `Task.Run()`. The UI now safely awaits the new `ManifestInitializationTask` during startup, guaranteeing the WinUI message pump is never frozen while files are being copied or parsed. 2. PowerToys Runner Watcher (Program.cs) - Old: Created a dedicated OS thread that blocked on a synchronous `runnerProcess.WaitForExit()` call, paired with a redundant global `WaitHandle` registration in App.xaml.cs. - New: Replaced with `Task.Run(async () => ...)` and `await runnerProcess.WaitForExitAsync()`. This frees the underlying thread while waiting for the runner to close. The legacy `ThreadPool.RegisterWaitForSingleObject` infrastructure was removed. 3. Activation Event Listener (App.xaml.cs) - Old: Used a raw `Thread` with a `while(true)` Win32 handle listener, which was stopped using `.Join(timeout)` during shutdown. - New: Migrated to `Task.Factory.StartNew(..., TaskCreationOptions.LongRunning)`. This preserves the dedicated background thread required for the blocking `WaitAny` loop, but standardises the lifecycle. It now shuts down cleanly using `Task.Wait()`, automatically catching any crashes inside a safe `AggregateException` rather than allowing unhandled thread exceptions to silently tear down the process. ### Miscellaneous - Added `AnonymizePath()` for logging paths, which replaces a user's username in a path with verbatim `` for privacy. - Index generation is now deterministic and independent of the order in which manifest files are retrieved. The same **index.yml** file will be produced for the same set of manifest files. ## Performance Release builds on Core i5-1135G7 laptop @ 2.4 GHz: **Old** 1075 ms (cold start, no files exist in destination folder) 965 ms (warm start, no files exist in destination folder) 902 ms (all manifest files exist, only index needs recreating) 892 ms (30 manifest files and index missing) 954 ms (index and all manifest files already present) **New** 117 ms (cold start no files exist in destination folder, copying files took 65 ms) 83 ms (warm start no files exist in destination folder, copying files took 60 ms) 37 ms (30 manifest files and index missing, 30 files copied in 35 ms) 27 ms (all manifest files exist, only index needs recreating) 6 ms (index and all manifest files already present) --- ## Validation Steps Performed - **Unit Tests**: - Added / updated `ShortcutGuide.UnitTests.IndexGeneratorTests` covering: - Standard manifest extraction - Quoted strings and unquoted values - Empty files and missing required properties (`PackageName`, `WindowFilter`) - Manifests with comments and trailing hashes - Reserved words, executable names with and without `.exe` - Case sensitivity and deterministic sorting - Index regeneration rules - All unit tests pass: - **Manual Verification**: - Verified overlay displays correct application shortcuts and dynamic PowerToys hotkeys. - Stress-tested rapid hotkey toggling to confirm the fix for the `_getAppIdsTask` `Dispose` bug. - Verified no visual flash / empty overlay box on first activation. - Verified user-added manifests in `%LocalAppData%\Microsoft\WinGet\KeyboardShortcuts` trigger re-indexing on the next launch. - Verified console output and file logging when invoking `PowerToys.ShortcutGuide.IndexYmlGenerator.exe` standalone. - Confirmed click-away behaviour and hotkey activation/deactivation work as before, and the overlay window appears in the foreground reliably.

title: [Keyboard Manager] Per-keyboard remap profiles (auto-switch + cycle hotkey)
body:
## Summary

Adds **per-keyboard remap profiles** to Keyboard Manager: keep several profiles and switch the active one based on which physical keyboard you're typing on.

Related to #12349 (and to #1460 / #35632) — but worth being precise, because that issue has collected two different asks over the years. Its original request is switching the **Windows keyboard layout** per device (US-Intl ↔ RUS, the way RightKeyboard does it), and this PR does **not** do that. What it implements is the other half the discussion converged on: per-device **remap profiles** with manual, automatic and hotkey switching — what @908875137 asked for there as "group management and a shortcut for quick switching". So there is deliberately no closing keyword here; #12349 should stay open for the layout case.

## Demo

Muted screen recording with on-screen captions:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbb35212-e5d8-4e45-838b-6413c10531f0

The clip shows two profiles — **"demo Type Cover"** and **"demo mac"** (the latter remaps `8 → 9`) — the **auto-switch** dialog identifying each keyboard by typing on it and assigning a profile, then live switching: typing on the **Type Cover** keeps `8` as `8`, switching to the **Apple keyboard** (`demo mac`) makes `8` become `9`, and the editor's profile picker follows the engine's auto-switch live. Known limitation shown: keys remapped by the *active* profile are suppressed by the low-level hook and never reach Raw Input, so auto-switch reacts to ordinary (non-remapped) keystrokes; the profile-cycle hotkey covers press-only-remapped-keys cases.

> The recording predates the storage rework and the toolbar layout below, so its editor screenshots are a version behind; the behaviour it shows is unchanged.

## What's included

**Engine (`KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary`)**
- `RawInputKeyboardTracker` — a dedicated hidden-window thread that uses Raw Input (`RIDEV_INPUTSINK`) to identify which physical keyboard produced each keystroke. It never suppresses input.
- Per-keyboard auto-switch in `KeyboardManager` — a `device -> profile` map plus an enable flag (`deviceProfiles.json`) drive switching the active profile. Switching reuses the existing settings-reload path (write `activeConfiguration` + signal the settings event), so remap state is never mutated off the reload thread. Device paths are matched on a normalized prefix (tolerant of instance-id churn seen on some virtual keyboards); injected input and modifier key-downs are excluded from the decision; a short hysteresis avoids thrashing.
- `ProfileCycleHotkey` — an optional global hotkey (`RegisterHotKey` + `MOD_NOREPEAT`) that cycles the active profile, as a reliable manual alternative to auto-switch.

**Editor (`KeyboardManagerEditorUI`)**
- Profile selector (create / delete / switch) in the list toolbar, built on the existing named-configuration mechanism.
- An **Auto-switch** dialog that identifies keyboards by having you type on them (`RawInputWatcher`), lets you assign a profile per keyboard, and writes `deviceProfiles.json`.

## How it works

Profiles are existing `{name}.json` config files listed in `keyboardConfigurations`; the active one is `activeConfiguration` in `settings.json`. Switching a profile writes that value and signals the engine's existing reload event — no new config plumbing.

## Editor storage: built on the model already in `main`

Following @niels9001's feedback, this PR **no longer keeps its own per-profile editor cache**. An earlier revision split `editorSettings.json` into `editorSettings.<profile>.json`, which duplicated the profile support `main` already has. It now uses that support directly:

- membership stays in `ShortcutSettings.Profiles` / `EditorSettings.ProfileDictionary`,
- the list is filtered by the existing `IsMappingInActiveProfile()`,
- switching a profile just runs the existing `ReconcileMappings(..., profileName)` against the newly loaded configuration.

Two things surfaced while doing this, and both are fixed here:

1. `KeyboardMappingService.ConfigurationName` is captured in the service constructor, and `SettingsManager` holds one service for the lifetime of the editor. With a profile picker in the UI, switching profiles with the editor open left that name stale, so a newly added remapping was tagged into the *previous* profile. `SettingsManager` now reads the active profile live (same source: `activeConfiguration`), and falls back to the old behaviour when the native service is unavailable.
2. `IsMappingInActiveProfile()` treats "no profiles" as "belongs everywhere" — correct for settings written before profiles existed. That means deleting a profile cannot simply untag its mappings, or they resurface in *every* profile. Deleting a profile now removes the mappings that belonged to it and to nothing else, and leaves never-tagged mappings alone.

Net effect on this PR: `SettingsManager.cs` gains two members and swaps four call sites instead of reworking the storage layer.

**Shared vs. copied remappings** — as discussed, the storage already expresses both, so this is a UI decision rather than a format one. With today's `ReconcileMappings`, duplicating a profile produces independent copies (the "hard copy" option) with no extra code, so that is what this PR ships. Sharing one remapping across profiles needs UI that doesn't exist yet (including an "update everywhere / only in this profile" prompt when editing a shared row) — happy to do that as a follow-up once we've settled the UX.

## Known limitation

Keys remapped by the *active* profile are suppressed by the low-level keyboard hook and therefore never reach Raw Input. So auto-switch reacts to ordinary (non-remapped) keystrokes; the profile-cycle hotkey covers cases where you only press remapped keys. This is documented in the code.

## Status / open items

- Rebased onto current `main` (post #49287); single commit, no conflicts.
- Profile picker lives in the KBM editor, per @niels9001. It shares the list toolbar rather than taking a row of its own, since the trailing filter cluster left that row's middle empty.
- Ready for review. The shared-vs-copied UX above is the one open design question, but per @niels9001's "I can help make tweaks to that later as well" it seemed better to get the mechanics reviewed and refine the UX on top, rather than keep the PR parked. Happy to put it back to draft if you'd rather settle that first.
- Auto-switch defaults to **off**; manual profile switching and the cycle hotkey are the primary paths.
- Editor UI for configuring the cycle hotkey is a follow-up (currently the definition lives in `deviceProfiles.json`).

## Testing

Built and exercised on a real machine (Apple Wireless Keyboard + Surface Type Cover) with a 6-profile, 84-remapping configuration:

- creating / switching / deleting profiles from the editor, assigning keyboards by typing, auto-switching on ordinary typing, and cycling profiles via the hotkey;
- engine-driven switches (auto-switch and the cycle hotkey) move the editor's picker and mapping list while it is open;
- a remapping added after switching profiles is tagged to the profile that is active at that moment (fix 1 above);
- deleting a profile removes exactly its own mappings — no leftover membership, no mappings orphaned into other profiles, and the operation-type index stays consistent (fix 2 above);
- "alone"/tap remaps (#49136) round-trip through the profile-aware reconcile unchanged.

title: Installer corrupts system PATH: DSCModules entry written with trailing quote, breaking cmd.exe executable lookup for subsequent PATH dirs
body:
### Brief bug description

The PowerToys installer writes a malformed entry into the **machine-wide PATH** (`HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment`): the new `C:\Program Files\PowerToys\DSCModules` entry is written with a **trailing double-quote** (`DSCModules"`).

This silently breaks executable name-lookup in cmd.exe for every PATH directory that appears *after* the malformed entry — including unrelated directories like `C:\Program Files\nodejs`. Symptoms are extremely misleading:

- `where <exe>` still finds the binary
- Python / PowerShell / MSYS see the PATH as containing the directory
- Direct execution by full path works
- Only bare-name invocation from cmd.exe (e.g. npm lifecycle scripts running `node ...`) fails with "'X' is not recognized as an internal or external command"

This cost several hours of misdiagnosis (Node.js reinstall suspected first) because every standard diagnostic tool reports the environment as healthy.

### Repro steps

Observed on an existing machine after PowerToys updated to 0.101.2362.0 on 2026-08-25. The registry value contained:

```
...;C:\ProgramData\chocolatey\bin;C:\Program Files\PowerToys\DSCModules";C:\Program Files\Nefarius Software Solutions\...;...;C:\Program Files\nodejs;...
```

Note the stray `"` after `DSCModules`. A second, correctly-formed `C:\Program Files\PowerToys\DSCModules\` entry also existed later in the value (appended by another install/update pass), so the broken entry appears to be from one installer code path while a corrected duplicate came from another.

After deleting the quoted entry via `reg.exe`, cmd.exe name lookup immediately started working again for all affected directories.

### Expected behavior

Installer appends `C:\Program Files\PowerToys\DSCModules` (no quote) to the system PATH exactly once.

### Actual behavior

A trailing `"` was embedded in the PATH value. Likely cause is an installer/environment-edit code path that quotes the path but fails to strip the surrounding quotes before concatenating into the REG_EXPAND_SZ value (or uses string formatting where the closing delimiter leaks into the stored data).

### Environment

- PowerToys version: 0.101.2362.0 (Preview)
- Install date: 2026-08-25
- Windows build: Insider 26300.2760 (Pro N)
- Affected: HKLM system PATH; any executables in PATH directories ordered after the malformed entry became unfindable by cmd.exe

### Suggested fix

Audit the PATH-write code paths (installer + any MSI/custom action that appends environment values): ensure the value is trimmed of surrounding quotes before being joined into PATH, and consider normalising/deduplicating entries on upgrade so a previously-corrupted value gets repaired.

title: ZoomIt: Fix LiveZoom taskbar duplication on Windows 11

labels.name: Product-ZoomIt
labels.description: Refers to the ZoomIt tool

body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

Fixes #48857.

On Windows 11, LiveZoom shows a second, unmagnified copy of the taskbar and of shell popups (Start, Search, Quick Settings, notification center, taskbar previews) on top of the zoomed view, which makes the taskbar unusable while LiveZoom is active.

Root cause: those shell surfaces live in z-bands above the desktop band, and explorer moves the taskbar itself into the Start band while they are open. The LiveZoom window is a topmost window in the desktop band, so it can never be above them.

Fix: signed builds embed a `uiAccess="true"` manifest, which places the LiveZoom window in the UIAccess band, above the shell bands (the same mechanism the On-Screen Keyboard uses). Unsigned builds are unchanged. DemoType gets an integrity check so uiAccess does not widen where it can type.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Closes: #48857
- [ ] **Communication:** I've discussed this with core contributors already. If the work hasn't been agreed, this work might be rejected
- [ ] **Tests:** Added/updated and all pass
- [ ] **Localization:** All end-user-facing strings can be localized
- [ ] **Dev docs:** Added/updated
- [ ] **New binaries:** Added on the required places
   - [ ] [JSON for signing](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/ESRPSigning_core.json) for new binaries
   - [ ] [WXS for installer](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/installer/PowerToysSetup/Product.wxs) for new binaries and localization folder
   - [ ] [YML for CI pipeline](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/ci/templates/build-powertoys-steps.yml) for new test projects
   - [x] [YML for signed pipeline](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/release.yml) (one property added to `.pipelines/v2/templates/job-build-project.yml`)
- [ ] **Documentation updated:** If checked, please file a pull request on [our docs repo](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/windows-uwp/tree/docs/hub/powertoys) and link it here: #xxx

No new binaries, no installer changes, no localized strings.

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

### Root cause (measured)

Measured with `GetWindowBand` + `EnumWindows`, `GetForegroundWindow` and `WindowFromPoint` probes while LiveZoom was active. Windows 11 build 26300.9457, single 3840x2160 monitor at 125%.

| Surface | Window | Band | Before fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| LiveZoom | `MagnifierClass` (ZoomIt) | 1 `ZBID_DESKTOP` | |
| Start / Search | `Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow` (StartMenuExperienceHost, SearchHost) | 6 `ZBID_IMMERSIVE_MOGO` | duplicate |
| Taskbar while Start, Quick Settings or notifications are open | `Shell_TrayWnd` | moves from 1 to **6** | duplicate taskbar |
| Quick Settings | `ControlCenterWindow` (ShellHost) | 4 `ZBID_IMMERSIVE_NOTIFICATION` | duplicate |
| Notification center | `Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow` (ShellExperienceHost) | 4 `ZBID_IMMERSIVE_NOTIFICATION` | duplicate |
| Tray overflow | `TopLevelWindowForOverflowXamlIsland` | 1 `ZBID_DESKTOP` | magnified correctly |

The tray overflow stays in the desktop band and is magnified correctly, which is consistent with the band explanation. The 10 ms `HWND_TOPMOST` reclaim in `LiveZoomWndProc` cannot help: z-order is only resolved within a band.

The On-Screen Keyboard (`osk.exe`, uiAccess) hit-tests above Start, Quick Settings and the notification center in the same setup, which confirms that `ZBID_UIACCESS` (2) stacks above bands 4 and 6.

### Changes

- `Zoomit.uiaccess.exe.manifest` (new): same as `Zoomit.exe.manifest`, plus `uiAccess="true"`.
- `binres.rc`: embeds the uiAccess manifest when `ZOOMIT_UIACCESS` is defined, otherwise the existing manifest.
- `ZoomIt.vcxproj`: defines `ZOOMIT_UIACCESS` for the resource compiler when the `ZoomItUIAccess` MSBuild property is `true`.
- `job-build-project.yml`: passes `/p:ZoomItUIAccess=${{ parameters.codeSign }}` to the main build, so only builds that get signed embed uiAccess.
- `DemoType.cpp`: `SendKeyInput` skips key-downs when the foreground window's process runs above the integrity level ZoomIt would have without uiAccess (medium unless ZoomIt is elevated), or when that level cannot be read. Key-ups always pass so modifiers never stick.

### Why gate on signing

A uiAccess binary must be signed with a trusted certificate. Measured on the same machine:

| Binary | Location | Result |
|---|---|---|
| unsigned, uiAccess manifest | any folder | fails to start: "A referral was returned from the server" |
| signed, uiAccess manifest | outside a secure location (e.g. `%LocalAppData%`) | starts, `TokenUIAccess=0`, behaves as today |
| signed, uiAccess manifest | `Program Files` | starts, `TokenUIAccess=1`, fix active |

So local and unsigned CI builds keep `asInvoker` (unchanged developer experience). Per-user installs start ZoomIt without uiAccess and behave exactly as today; the fix applies to per-machine installs. Measured at UAC `ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin` 0 and 5 with an admin account.

### Why the DemoType check

A uiAccess process is exempt from UIPI, and on this machine a non-elevated uiAccess ZoomIt runs at high integrity (`0x3000`). Without the check, DemoType could type into elevated windows, which it cannot do today. The check keeps its reach the same as before.

### Why this differs from the original Sysinternals decision

The comment above the `g_fullScreenWorkaround` check notes uiAccess was impractical for ZoomIt because the exe has to be copied under `%ProgramFiles%`. Standalone Sysinternals ZoomIt runs from wherever it was downloaded. PowerToys per-machine installs already put a signed ZoomIt in Program Files, so the requirement is met without extra steps for users.

## Validation Steps Performed

Windows 11 26H2 build 26300.9457, single monitor (3840x2160 at 125%). Prototype signed with a temporary trusted test certificate and run from `C:\Program Files\ZoomItProto`, default ZoomIt hotkeys.

Bands with the fix (LiveZoom active):

| Surface | ZoomIt window band | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| LiveZoom only | 2 `ZBID_UIACCESS` | normal |
| Start | 2 | single magnified view, no duplicate |
| Quick Settings | 2 | single magnified view |
| Notification center | 2 | single magnified view |
| Taskbar icon hover preview | 2 | single magnified view |
| Tray overflow | 2 | normal |
| Elevated launch (`Elevated=1`, `UIAccess=1`), Start | 2 | single magnified view |

The taskbar also keeps `WS_EX_TOPMOST` while LiveZoom is active with the fix; before, it lost it and dropped to the bottom of the desktop band.

Checklist:

- [x] Ctrl+4 enter/exit: unchanged, no added UI or delay
- [x] Clicks into Start, Quick Settings and flyouts while zoomed land correctly; no flicker observed
- [x] Ctrl+1 static zoom, Ctrl+2 draw, Ctrl+3 break timer
- [x] Ctrl+5 recording while LiveZoomed: saved file shows the magnified view
- [x] Windows Magnifier running at the same time
- [x] LiveDraw over LiveZoom: same behavior with and without uiAccess (1 missed stroke in 10 on both builds; pre-existing)
- [x] DemoType (Ctrl+7) into normal Notepad: types (`target=0x2000 limit=0x2000`)
- [x] DemoType into elevated Notepad: nothing typed (`target=0x3000 limit=0x2000`), same as today
- [x] Build: default and `/p:ZoomItUIAccess=False` embed `asInvoker`; `/p:ZoomItUIAccess=True` embeds `uiAccess="true"`; no new warnings

Not covered:

- Multi-monitor and mixed DPI (single monitor available)
- Standard (non-admin) user account
- A per-machine install launched by the runner (test machine has a per-user install; launches were standalone, elevated and non-elevated)
- Webcam preview and DemoMirror
- ZoomIt UI tests (`src/modules/ZoomIt/Tests/ZoomIt.UITests`): need WinAppDriver and Developer Mode, not run
- The flicker described in the issue did not reproduce on the test machine before or after the fix
- The final commit was built and its manifest verified; the end-to-end runs used builds with the same code (one with temporary logging for the DemoType checks)

To test locally: build ZoomIt with `/p:ZoomItUIAccess=true`, sign `PowerToys.ZoomIt.exe` with a certificate trusted in `LocalMachine\Root`, copy it under `Program Files` and run it from there.

body:
### __Description of the new feature / enhancement__

While the new **Window Hopper** tool is great, I really wouldn't mind having the opposite of it as well: an **App Hopper**.

Pressing a shortcut would make you **switch focus from the currently-active program to the other programs**, sorted by most recently active. It would work like alt-tab or Window Hopper when the shortcut is pressed. 

If the hopped-to program had several windows then it would default to focusing on the most recently-used window.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When I'm switching between several browser windows and now suddenly want to go to Discord without having to press alt-tab 5 times. But there can be MANY use case scenarios.

### Supporting information

Maybe it could be called the Program Hopper. 

Importantly, this **shouldn't be a new PowerToy** but both the Window Hopper and this App Hopper should be **combined into one single "Hopper" PowerToy**. There you could set all the settings for both Window Hopper and for App Hopper, **including** setting each of them on/off independently. 

There should be an off-by-default option to only show program icons and not previews of the window that will be selected when you're App Hopping.
